title: Lifting a set-sheaf equivalence to complete category-valued sheaves
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(C,J)$ and $(D,K)$ be $\mathcal V$-small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], whose topologies are subcanonical, meaning that every representable $h_c=\operatorname{Hom}_C(-,c)$ and $h_d=\operatorname{Hom}_D(-,d)$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal V$-sets. Let $u:C\to D$ preserve finite limits and coverings. Suppose restriction
$$R_{\mathrm{set}}:\operatorname{Sh}(D,K;\mathrm{Sets}_{\mathcal V})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}(C,J;\mathrm{Sets}_{\mathcal V}),\qquad H\longmapsto H\circ u^{\mathrm{op}}$$
is an equivalence. Let $\mathcal A$ be a locally $\mathcal V$-small category admitting all $\mathcal V$-small limits: every diagram indexed by a category with objects and arrows in $\mathcal V$ has a limit in $\mathcal A$. An $\mathcal A$-valued presheaf $F$ is a sheaf precisely when $c\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(a,F(c))$ is a sheaf of sets for every $a\in\mathcal A$. Then restriction
$$R_{\mathcal A}:\operatorname{Sh}(D,K;\mathcal A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}(C,J;\mathcal A),\qquad F\longmapsto F\circ u^{\mathrm{op}}$$
is an equivalence of categories.

proof.text: Put $L=u^{\mathrm{op}}$. For each $d\in D$, the comma category $(d\downarrow L)$, with $d$ viewed in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$, is $I_d=(u\downarrow d)^{\mathrm{op}}$: its underlying pairs are $(c,\alpha:u(c)\to d)$. Its objects and arrows form $\mathcal V$-sets, since $C,D$ are $\mathcal V$-small. The cited pointwise Kan lemma therefore constructs $T_{\mathcal A}$ and $T_{\mathrm{set}}$ on presheaves, with $(TF)(d)=\lim_{I_d}F(c)$ and precomposition adjunction $P\dashv T$. These are limits over $I_d$, never over a whole sheaf category.

source.place: Tag 00VR (definition-sheaf), Hom-test; agent argument using pointwise right Kan extension and Yoneda (categories.tex lemma-yoneda).

proof.text:
First check the set-valued inverse. Choose a quasi-inverse $E$ to the given $R_{\mathrm{set}}$, with $R_{\mathrm{set}}EF\cong F$. For a set sheaf $F$ on $C$, subcanonicity and Yoneda give
$$ (EF)(d)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(h_d,EF)\cong\operatorname{Nat}(R_{\mathrm{set}}h_d,F). $$
The second bijection is full faithfulness of the given equivalence followed by $R_{\mathrm{set}}EF\cong F$. Write a transformation in the last set as the family $x_{c,\alpha}\in F(c)$ obtained by evaluating its $c$-component at $\alpha:u(c)\to d$. Naturality is exactly $F(g)x_{c,\alpha}=x_{c',\alpha u(g)}$ for $g:c'\to c$. Thus these transformations are precisely the compatible families defining $\lim_{I_d}F(c)$, including when $I_d$ is empty. This gives $EF\cong T_{\mathrm{set}}F$, naturally in $d$ and $F$: an arrow $d'\to d$ reindexes $\alpha$ by composition, and a morphism $F\to F'$ acts on each $x_{c,\alpha}$. Hence $T_{\mathrm{set}}F$ is a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 00VR (definition-sheaf), Hom-test; agent argument using pointwise right Kan extension and Yoneda (categories.tex lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Restriction of an $\mathcal A$-sheaf is an $\mathcal A$-sheaf: its $H_a$-test is $R_{\mathrm{set}}(H_aF)$, a sheaf by hypothesis. Conversely, for an $\mathcal A$-sheaf $F$ on $C$, the Hom/Kan comparison gives $H_a(T_{\mathcal A}F)\cong T_{\mathrm{set}}(H_aF)$ for every $a$. The latter is a sheaf by step 2. The Hom-test in the statement now proves that $T_{\mathcal A}F$ is a sheaf. Thus both presheaf adjunctions restrict to the full subcategories of sheaves, with exactly the same units and counits.

source.place: Tag 00VR (definition-sheaf), Hom-test; agent argument using pointwise right Kan extension and Yoneda (categories.tex lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: For sets the restricted adjunction has left adjoint $R_{\mathrm{set}}$, an equivalence. Its counit $\epsilon^{\mathrm{set}}_F:R_{\mathrm{set}}T_{\mathrm{set}}F\to F$ is therefore invertible by the cited adjunction lemma. For an $\mathcal A$-sheaf $F$, the counit equation of the Hom/Kan comparison identifies $H_a(\epsilon^{\mathcal A}_{F,c})$ with $\epsilon^{\mathrm{set}}_{H_aF,c}\circ\chi_{F,u(c)}$. Both factors are bijections. The cited Hom-detection criterion, applied in $\mathcal A$ for all $a$, shows that every component $\epsilon^{\mathcal A}_{F,c}$ is invertible. Component inverses form a natural inverse, so $\epsilon^{\mathcal A}_F$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 00VR (definition-sheaf), Hom-test; agent argument using pointwise right Kan extension and Yoneda (categories.tex lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: Restriction $R_{\mathcal A}$ reflects isomorphisms. Indeed, if $R_{\mathcal A}(v)$ is invertible then for every $a$, $R_{\mathrm{set}}(H_a(v))=H_a(R_{\mathcal A}(v))$ is invertible. An equivalence reflects isomorphisms: full faithfulness lifts the inverse and faithfulness verifies its two inverse identities. Thus $H_a(v)$ is invertible for all $a$. Applying Hom-detection at each object of $D$ shows that $v$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 00VR (definition-sheaf), Hom-test; agent argument using pointwise right Kan extension and Yoneda (categories.tex lemma-yoneda).

proof.text: For a sheaf $G$ on $D$, the triangle identity is $\epsilon^{\mathcal A}_{R_{\mathcal A}G}\circ R_{\mathcal A}(\eta^{\mathcal A}_G)=1_{R_{\mathcal A}G}$. The counit is invertible by step 4, hence $R_{\mathcal A}(\eta^{\mathcal A}_G)$ is its inverse. Step 5 implies that $\eta^{\mathcal A}_G$ is invertible. The natural isomorphisms $\eta^{\mathcal A}:1\cong T_{\mathcal A}R_{\mathcal A}$ and $\epsilon^{\mathcal A}:R_{\mathcal A}T_{\mathcal A}\cong1$ exhibit $T_{\mathcal A}$ as a quasi-inverse of the actual restriction functor in the statement.
